items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Then there was Jimmy Lunceford's That was (unintelligible) reed section.

ctx.x: Now, I'm saying that, look like I'm a diehard, because music moves on. It's true. But I love beautiful sounds. I love beautiful sounds. I was listening recently to a whole old

Duke Ellington 1940s band, the reeds section of Hodges, Otto Hardwick, Ben Webster, Harry Carney, Barney Bigard, -- to me, that was one of the greatest reed sections in the world. Then there was Jimmy Lunceford's That was (unintelligible) reed section. Another terrible reed section -- But, Thad and eh, but bad and Mel's reed section, very beautiful. It has been. But I don't know, like you say, where music is heading. It's hard to say. I'm going to go back a little bit.

I came down here -- I think it was '61 -- with Al Gray and Billy Mitchell. They had a sextet. We had a week at Peps, old Peps down there on Broad Street. He had a trumpet player -- I forgot the brother's name -- he also had arranger, Gene, who played piano as well as peck horn. That's an alto horn, looks something like your that euphonium that Kiane plays (unintelligible). But it blended, so that meant we had four horns and his drums and bass on certain arrangements. It was beautiful, beautiful sound. I stayed…
